scan_ocr_evidence.verification_basis: Authenticated repository ledgers control exact wording and marks; the 2026 official scan identity is additionally hash-recorded. Absence of separately located older scan files is recorded, not concealed.

wording_notes.2026_Q5c: Ledger-normalized wording uses “Sankhya”; authenticated printed OCR/scan wording reads “Sarnkhya”.

primary.question: Q5(e)
primary.exact_wording: Is Puruṣa one or many? Explain the Sāṃkhya position in this regard and give arguments in support of your answer.
primary.demand_decoding: State numerical plurality; present the three Kārikā arguments first; add liberation only as a supplementary inference; evaluate individuation.

primary.question: Q7(b)
primary.exact_wording: How do the Advaita Vedāntins react to the Prakṛtipariṇāmavāda of the Sāṃkhya philosophy? How do the Sāṃkhyas defend their own position in this regard? Discuss.
primary.demand_decoding: Contrast real transformation with apparent transformation; reconstruct Śaṅkara’s objections; present Sāṃkhya replies and a graded verdict.

primary.question: Q5(d)
primary.exact_wording: Critically discuss the metaphysical status of a Jīva and a Puruṣa according to Sāṃkhya philosophy.
primary.demand_decoding: Distinguish metaphysical Puruṣa from empirical jīva, explain reflection and transmigration, then expose the bondage paradox.

primary.question: Q8(c)
primary.exact_wording: Which Sāṃkhya proof for the existence of Prakṛti actually shows that there can be only one Prakṛti? Justify your answer.
primary.demand_decoding: Identify avibhāgāt vaiśvarūpyasya, distinguish it from the other four proofs, and test whether unity follows demonstratively.

primary.question: Q7(a)
primary.exact_wording: “A mango tree is grown out of a mango seed.” How will Sāṃkhya system explain this process through their theory of causation by rejecting their rival perspectives?
primary.demand_decoding: Apply all five satkāryavāda arguments to seed-tree continuity and reject Nyāya, Advaita and Buddhist alternatives.

primary.question: Q6(b)
primary.exact_wording: Explain the Sāṃkhya view on three guṇas (guṇa-traya) and their modifications.
primary.demand_decoding: Define the guṇas as constituents, explain cooperation and equilibrium, distinguish sarūpa from virūpa pariṇāma, and evaluate.

primary.question: Q5(a)
primary.exact_wording: Examine and evaluate the proofs given by Sāṃkhya philosophy to prove the existence of Puruṣa.
primary.demand_decoding: Explain all five cumulative proofs, identify sāmānyato-dṛṣṭa inference, distinguish proof of subjectivity from proof of plurality, and evaluate.

primary.question: Q5(b)
primary.exact_wording: “If Puruṣa and Prakṛti are two completely independent realities, then no relation between the two is possible.” In the light of this statement make a brief presentation of Śaṅkara’s criticism of Sāṃkhya dualism.
primary.demand_decoding: Present Śaṅkara’s dilemma about two independent principles, test Sāṃkhya’s proximity and analogies, and conclude briefly.

primary.question: Q7(a)
primary.exact_wording: Present an account of evolution of Prakṛti as propounded in Sāṃkhyakārikā. In this context, also explain the difference between buddhi, mahat and ahaṃkāra.
primary.demand_decoding: Give the exact ordered 25-tattva sequence, distinguish branches, and clarify that mahat and buddhi are one tattva while ahaṃkāra is its evolute.

primary.question: Q7(a)
primary.exact_wording: Why does Śaṅkara consider Sāṃkhya Philosophy as his chief opponent (pradhāna malla)? Examine his arguments against Sāṃkhya Philosophy.
primary.demand_decoding: Explain why Sāṃkhya is the strongest systematic rival, present Śaṅkara’s scriptural and rational objections, replies, and residual comparison.

primary.question: Q5(c)
primary.exact_wording: Is Purusa one or many? Explain and examine the Sankhya position in this context.
primary.demand_decoding: Answer one-or-many directly, explain the classical grounds, then examine both Advaita and internal objections.

primary.question: Q6(a)
primary.exact_wording: "A mango tree is grown out of a mango seed." How do the Sankhya philosophers explain this process through their theory of causation by rejecting their rival perspectives?
primary.demand_decoding: Use the mango case to explain latent determinacy and pariṇāma, then answer rival asatkārya, vivarta and dependent-origination accounts.

supporting.question: Q5(a)
supporting.exact_wording: Does the seed contain the tree? Discuss with reference to Nyāya-Vaiśeṣika Philosophy.
supporting.route: Primary owner: Nyāya–Vaiśeṣika; Sāṃkhya supplies the satkāryavāda contrast only.

supporting.question: Q5(e)
supporting.exact_wording: Do you agree with the view that ‘Vivartavāda is the logical development of Pariṇāmavāda’? Give reasons in support of your answer.
supporting.route: Primary owner: Vedānta; Sāṃkhya supplies the pariṇāma comparison only.

supporting.question: Q8(b)
supporting.exact_wording: Write a note on Nyāya notion of Prāgabhāva (prior non-existence). How does this notion help Naiyāyikas in defending their position on causation against the Sāṃkhya view of causation? Critically discuss.
supporting.route: Primary owner: Nyāya–Vaiśeṣika; Sāṃkhya supplies the satkāryavāda comparison only.

originals.question: Explain why Sāṃkhya restricts the means of valid knowledge to three, and show how this restriction shapes its metaphysics.
"Nothing happens to Puruṣa at liberation." Comment on this statement with reference to the Sāṃkhya account of bondage and kaivalya.
Examine the claim that Sāṃkhya's theory of the three qualities makes cosmology and psychology a single subject.
Critically examine whether the Sāṃkhya doctrine of many Puruṣas is proved or merely postulated.
Analyse the relation between Sāṃkhya's epistemology, its theory of causation and its account of liberation, and assess whether the three form a coherent system.
"Sāṃkhya purchases the inactivity of consciousness at a high price." Discuss with reference to agency, moral responsibility and rebirth.
